Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

content.text:
**Finding: Compliant** — no redline proposed.

Section 18 (¶ p0068–p0069) already delivers our preferred insurance package, binding on Cobalt Cloud Services LLC:

| Playbook requirement | Document |
|---|---|
| CGL USD 1M/occ, 2M agg | ✅ USD 1,000,000 / 2,000,000 |
| Professional (E&O) USD 2M | ✅ USD 2,000,000 |
| Cyber/privacy USD 5M (processes Customer Data) | ✅ USD 5,000,000 |
| Workers' compensation as required by law | ✅ plus employer's liability USD 1M |
| Certificates on request | ✅ § 18.2 |

Additional favorable terms beyond the playbook: a one-year post-term tail, reputable-insurer and primary-coverage requirements, advance notice of cancellation or material reduction, and express confirmation that insurance does not limit Vendor's liabilities (preserving the Section 21.3 Excluded Claims exposure). Given Juniper Ridge's health-data profile, the USD 5M cyber layer sits at our preferred level rather than the fallback, so no escalation is needed.

input.quote: 2.1 Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.
input.rationale: No express "liquidated damages" or penalty clause exists, and the only service-credit reference (1.5) runs in our favour. However, Section 2.1 is a disguised Customer-payable liquidated amount: it fixes USD 2,000,000 per year (USD 6,000,000 total) payable on a take-or-pay basis "without reduction or termination rights", so we would owe the full remaining contract value for Services never consumed even after terminating for Vendor breach. That exceeds the walk-away threshold (liquidated amounts equal to remaining contract value) and conflicts with 7.1 (no unstated minimum-use charge), 12.3 (no minimum-volume commitment) and 27.3 (termination "without penalty"). The redline removes the binding minimum and states that no take-or-pay, penalty, liquidated damages, or early-termination amount is payable by Customer, with a three-months'-Fees early-termination fee offered as fallback.

proposal.summary: Remove the Customer-payable take-or-pay/minimum-fee liability in 2.1 and confirm no liquidated damages, penalty, or early-termination fee is payable by Customer.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have converted the take-or-pay commitment in 2.1 into a non-binding volume expectation, because as drafted it obliges us to pay up to USD 6,000,000 for Services we may never receive and strips our reduction and termination rights, which is a liquidated damages/penalty payable by Customer that our playbook does not accept. If Cobalt needs some downside protection, we can discuss a single early-termination fee capped at three months' Fees as the sole liquidated amount.

Parties: we represent Juniper Ridge Health, Inc.; counterparty is Cobalt Cloud Services LLC.

Rule:
ID: LD
Title: Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer
Kind: direction
Summary: Service credits to us are welcome; liquidated damages against us are not.
Severity: high
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer.
Position — fallback:
Early-termination fee capped at 3 months' fees as the sole liquidated amount.
Position — walk-away:
Liquidated damages exceeding the remaining contract value or triggered by minor breaches.
Detection guidance:
Identify liquidated damages, penalties, minimum fees on termination, "shall pay … as liquidated damages". Flag only when Customer pays. Service credits or LDs payable by Vendor to Customer are compliant.

Redline guidance:
Delete the Customer-payable LD; if an early-termination fee is unavoidable, cap it at 3 months' fees.

input.quote: 2.1 Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.
input.rationale: No express "liquidated damages" or penalty clause exists, and the only service-credit reference (1.5) runs in our favour. However, Section 2.1 is a disguised Customer-payable liquidated amount: it fixes USD 2,000,000 per year (USD 6,000,000 total) payable on a take-or-pay basis "without reduction or termination rights", so we would owe the full remaining contract value for Services never consumed even after terminating for Vendor breach. That exceeds the walk-away threshold (liquidated amounts equal to remaining contract value) and conflicts with 7.1 (no unstated minimum-use charge), 12.3 (no minimum-volume commitment) and 27.3 (termination "without penalty"). The redline removes the binding minimum and states that no take-or-pay, penalty, liquidated damages, or early-termination amount is payable by Customer, with a three-months'-Fees early-termination fee offered as fallback.

**Finding: Compliant** — no redline proposed.

Section 19 already delivers our preferred warranty package:

- **19.1** — Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner by qualified personnel to industry standards, plus material conformity to documentation and specifications.
- **19.2** — Deliverables conform for ninety days from the later of delivery or acceptance; hosted Services conform *throughout the subscription term*, which exceeds our 12-month software benchmark.
- **19.3** — No malicious code and compliance with Applicable Law, plus a no-functionality-degradation and open-source-contamination warranty.
- **19.4** — Real remedy: prompt re-performance, repair or replacement at no charge, escalating to termination and refund of Fees paid, and expressly non-exclusive for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security and indemnified claims.
- **19.5** — The disclaimer is confined to implied warranties and expressly preserves express warranties, service levels, indemnities and stated remedies, so it does not erode the bargain.

Only observation for the file: the malicious-code warranty is limited to code "intentionally introduced by Vendor." That is market-standard and is backstopped by the Section 17 security program obligations, so we would not spend negotiating capital on it.

Parties: we represent Juniper Ridge Health, Inc.; counterparty is Cobalt Cloud Services LLC.

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

content.text:
**Finding submitted: deviation (high severity), Section 2.1 (p0012).**

What I checked and found:
- No express "liquidated damages" or penalty language anywhere in the body; searches for "liquidated damages", "penalt", and termination-for-convenience fees returned nothing adverse (the only "penalty" hit, 27.3, benefits us).
- Service credits are referenced only in the Fees definition (1.5) and run in our favour — compliant.
- The real exposure is **2.1's take-or-pay**: USD 2,000,000 per year for three years (USD 6,000,000) payable "without reduction or termination rights." That is a Customer-payable liquidated amount equal to the full remaining contract value, owed even for Services never consumed and even after we terminate for Cobalt's breach — squarely in the walk-away band. It also conflicts with 7.1 (no unstated minimum-use charge), 12.3 (Customer has made no minimum-volume commitment) and 27.3 (termination "without penalty").

Redline (validated ok:true): converts the binding minimum into a non-binding volume expectation, confirms we pay only for Services actually ordered, and states that no take-or-pay charge, shortfall, minimum fee, penalty, liquidated damages, or early-termination fee is payable by Customer, with reduction/termination rights preserved. The comment offers the playbook fallback of a single early-termination fee capped at three months' Fees.

input.rationale: § 2.1 imposes a multi-year take-or-pay commitment on us (USD 2,000,000 per year for three years) expressly "without reduction or termination rights" — the playbook walk-away position. It also conflicts with § 12.3, where Vendor acknowledges we have made no minimum-volume commitment. We replaced it with the preferred position (fees for Services ordered or used only), and offered the 12-month, reducible, true-up fallback in the comment.

Parties: we represent Juniper Ridge Health, Inc.; counterparty is Cobalt Cloud Services LLC.

Rule:
ID: MINCOMMIT
Title: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not take-or-pay without an exit.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.
Position — fallback:
Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
Position — walk-away:
Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.
Detection guidance:
"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.
Redline guidance:

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

Finding submitted.

**Deviation — MINCOMMIT (§ 2.1, p0012).** The clause imposes a three-year, USD 2,000,000/year take-or-pay commitment on us with no reduction or termination right — the playbook walk-away scenario — and it directly contradicts § 12.3, where Vendor acknowledges we have made no minimum-volume commitment (and § 7.1's bar on undisclosed minimum-use charges).

Redline (validated, preferred level): § 2.1 replaced so that we have no minimum purchase, volume, or take-or-pay commitment and pay only for Services actually ordered or used. The comment flags the § 12.3 inconsistency and offers the fallback (12-month commitment, reducible on 30 days' notice, true-up not penalty) if a commitment is commercially essential.

input.quote: 10.1 On expiry or termination, Customer's right to access terminated subscription Services ends after any agreed transition period. Rights in accepted Deliverables, paid-up licences, Customer Data, and materials Customer owned or licensed independently continue according to their terms.
input.rationale: Section 10 (Effect of Expiry or Termination) addresses only access cut-off, Deliverable delivery and refunds. There is no obligation on Vendor to provide transition assistance, and no Customer Data return/export or deletion-certification obligation anywhere in the Agreement: searches for "transition", "machine-readable", "delet" and "return" surface only the passing reference to "any agreed transition period" in 10.1 (which presupposes an agreement that does not exist) and Section 16.5, which expressly carves Customer Data out to "Sections 11 and 15" — Section 11 does not exist in the document and Section 15 contains no return or deletion duty. In a hosted-services agreement this absence is a deviation under the playbook, so we insert a new Section 10.3 with the model language: up to six months of transition assistance at Vendor's then-current rates, return of Customer Data in a commonly used machine-readable format within 30 days, and certified deletion thereafter (fallback: 90 days of assistance with the same 30-day export).

Parties: we represent Juniper Ridge Health, Inc.; counterparty is Cobalt Cloud Services LLC.

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

content.content: [{"id":"sec-p0000","heading":"MASTER SERVICES AGREEMENT","level":1,"paragraphCount":2},{"id":"sec-1","number":"1","heading":"DEFINITIONS","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-1.1","number":"1.1","heading":"“Affiliate” means, with respect to a Party, any entity that directly or indirectly controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with that Party. “Control” means ownership of more than fifty percent of the voting interests of an entity or the power to direct its management. An entity is an Affiliate only while that relationship continues.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-1.2","number":"1.2","heading":"“Applicable Law” means every statute, regulation, binding regulatory requirement, court order, and governmental rule applicable to a Party's performance under this Agreement, including laws concerning privacy, information security, export controls, employment, anti-bribery, and accessibility. Applicable Law does not include a private standard unless an Order Form expressly adopts it.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-1.3","number":"1.3","heading":"“Customer Data” means all data, records, files, content, personal information, and other materials submitted to, stored in, transmitted through, or otherwise made available to the Services by or for Customer or its Authorized Users, together with output specifically derived from that material. Customer Data excludes anonymized operational telemetry that cannot reasonably be linked to Customer, an Authorized User, or an individual.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-1.4","number":"1.4","heading":"“Deliverable” means each report, configuration, integration, specification, design, workflow, training material, and other work product that an Order Form identifies as being created specifically for Customer. Deliverables exclude Vendor Technology and generally applicable ideas, methods, skills, and know-how retained in the unaided memory of Vendor personnel.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-1.5","number":"1.5","heading":"“Fees” means the recurring subscription fees, professional services fees, usage fees, and other amounts payable by Customer under an Order Form for the Services during the applicable period. Fees do not include taxes, reimbursable expenses, service credits, interest, damages, or a one-time implementation charge unless an Order Form expressly states otherwise.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-1.6","number":"1.6","heading":"“Order Form” means a written ordering document signed by authorized representatives of both Parties that references this Agreement and describes the Services, Deliverables, subscription quantities, service levels, Fees, and term purchased by Customer. A purchase order is an administrative convenience only and does not amend an Order Form or this Agreement.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-1.7","number":"1.7","heading":"“Services” means the hosted software, implementation, configuration, support, maintenance, consulting, and related services described in an Order Form. Services include all corrections, updates, and generally released improvements Vendor provides without an additional licence fee to similarly situated customers purchasing the same service tier.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-1.8","number":"1.8","heading":"“Vendor Technology” means Vendor's pre-existing software, tools, models, templates, documentation, routines, connectors, and other technology, and modifications of them that are not Deliverables and do not embody Customer Confidential Information. Vendor Technology does not include Customer Data or intellectual property owned by Customer before the Effective Date.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-2","number":"2","heading":"AGREEMENT STRUCTURE AND SCOPE","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-2.1","number":"2.1","heading":"Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-2.2","number":"2.2","heading":"Each Order Form is governed by this Agreement. If provisions conflict, the following order controls: a signed amendment that expressly identifies the provision amended; the applicable Order Form; any service-level exhibit; any security exhibit; and this Agreement. An Order Form prevails only for that Order Form and only when it expressly identifies the conflicting provision.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-2.3","number":"2.3","heading":"Vendor terms appearing on a website, click-through screen, invoice, quotation, acknowledgement, support portal, or purchase-order response do not apply, even if access to the Services technically requires acceptance. Customer's use of or payment for Services does not assent to additional or different terms.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-3","number":"3","heading":"SERVICES AND PERFORMANCE","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-3.1","number":"3.1","heading":"Vendor shall provide the Services professionally, diligently, and in accordance with this Agreement, each Order Form, the documentation, agreed project plans, and Applicable Law. Vendor is responsible for the acts and omissions of its personnel, Affiliates, and subcontractors as though they were Vendor's own.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-4","number":"4","heading":"ORDER FORMS AND AFFILIATE ORDERS","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-4.1","number":"4.1","heading":"An Order Form becomes binding when signed by both Parties. Changes in scope, assumptions, quantities, Fees, dependencies, or dates require a written change order signed by authorized representatives. Vendor shall not charge for work outside scope that Customer did not approve in a signed change order.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-5","number":"5","heading":"IMPLEMENTATION AND CHANGE CONTROL","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-5.1","number":"5.1","heading":"Vendor shall prepare and maintain an implementation plan identifying tasks, owners, assumptions, dependencies, deliverables, acceptance criteria, risks, and target dates. The Parties will hold regular status meetings during implementation. Vendor shall keep accurate action and decision logs and furnish them to Customer on request.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-6","number":"6","heading":"ACCEPTANCE","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-6.1","number":"6.1","heading":"Customer will have fifteen business days after delivery of a Deliverable to test it against the acceptance criteria in the applicable Order Form. Customer may accept it in writing or reject it by describing material nonconformities. Payment, productive use needed for testing, or silence does not constitute acceptance.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-6.2","number":"6.2","heading":"If Customer rejects a Deliverable, Vendor shall promptly correct the nonconformities at no additional charge and resubmit it for a new acceptance period. Each invoice must identify the Order Form, period, Services, quantities, applicable credits, and a valid purchase-order number if Customer supplied one. Proper undisputed invoices are due forty-five days after receipt.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-7.3","number":"7.3","heading":"Customer may withhold a genuinely disputed amount by notifying Vendor before its due date and explaining the basis. The Parties will work promptly and in good faith to resolve the dispute. Vendor shall continue the Services while a payment dispute is pending and shall not charge interest on an amount ultimately found not due.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-7.4","number":"7.4","heading":"Fees exclude sales, use, value-added, and similar transaction taxes that Vendor is legally required to collect and separately states on a valid invoice. Customer is not responsible for taxes on Vendor's income, property, payroll, personnel, or franchise, or for taxes avoidable through Vendor's timely use of a valid exemption certificate.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-7.5","number":"7.5","heading":"Pre-approved travel expenses are reimbursable at cost without markup and in accordance with Customer's travel policy. Vendor shall provide receipts and request reimbursement within sixty days. All other expenses are included in the Fees.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-8","number":"8","heading":"TERM AND RENEWAL","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-8.1","number":"8.1","heading":"This Agreement begins on the Effective Date and continues for three years unless earlier terminated in accordance with its terms. Expiration of this Agreement does not itself terminate an Order Form then in effect; this Agreement continues to govern that Order Form until the Order Form expires or is terminated.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-8.2","number":"8.2","heading":"Each Order Form has the initial term stated in it and thereafter renews for successive twelve-month periods unless Customer gives Vendor at least thirty days' written notice of non-renewal. Vendor shall remind Customer of an upcoming renewal at least sixty days beforehand. Failure to send the reminder extends Customer's opt-out deadline until thirty days after the reminder is received.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-8.3","number":"8.3","heading":"On renewal, Vendor may increase recurring Fees only by the lesser of the increase in the United States Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers during the preceding twelve months and three percent. Vendor must give at least ninety days' written notice of an increase. No increase applies to prepaid periods.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-9","number":"9","heading":"TERMINATION","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-9.1","number":"9.1","heading":"Either Party may terminate this Agreement or an affected Order Form for the other Party's material breach if the breach remains uncured thirty days after written notice describing it in reasonable detail. If a breach cannot reasonably be cured within thirty days, the cure period extends up to sixty additional days while the breaching Party diligently pursues cure.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-9.2","number":"9.2","heading":"Either Party may terminate immediately by written notice if the other becomes insolvent, makes a general assignment for creditors, enters liquidation, or becomes subject to a bankruptcy proceeding not dismissed within sixty days. A lawful reorganization that does not impair performance is not, by itself, grounds for termination.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-9.3","number":"9.3","heading":"Customer may terminate an Order Form immediately if Vendor suffers a material Security Incident, repeatedly misses a critical service level, violates Applicable Law in performing the Services, or infringes a third party's intellectual property and cannot provide the remedies required by Section 20.5.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-9.5","number":"9.5","heading":"Termination of one Order Form does not terminate another Order Form unless Customer states that the affected Services are operationally inseparable. A termination right is in addition to, and does not exclude, any other remedy available under this Agreement or Applicable Law.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-10","number":"10","heading":"EFFECT OF EXPIRY OR TERMINATION","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-10.1","number":"10.1","heading":"On expiry or termination, Customer's right to access terminated subscription Services ends after any agreed transition period. Rights in accepted Deliverables, paid-up licences, Customer Data, and materials Customer owned or licensed independently continue according to their terms.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-10.2","number":"10.2","heading":"Vendor shall deliver all completed and in-process Deliverables for which Customer has paid or agrees to pay the applicable proportionate Fees. Vendor shall refund prepaid recurring Fees covering the period after termination, together with Fees paid for Services Customer cannot reasonably use because of Vendor's uncured breach.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-12","number":"12","heading":"CUSTOMER RESPONSIBILITIES","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-12.3","number":"12.3","heading":"Nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling, or using any product or service, engaging any supplier, hiring any person who responds to general recruitment, or conducting business in any field or territory. Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-12.4","number":"12.4","heading":"Customer shall not solicit, hire, or employ any Vendor employee during the term or for twenty-four months afterward, regardless of how the employee applies.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-12.4-2","number":"12.4","heading":"During the term and for twenty-four months thereafter, Customer shall not develop, market, sell, or acquire any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-13","number":"13","heading":"ACCESS RIGHTS AND LICENCE","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-13.1","number":"13.1","heading":"Subject to payment of applicable Fees, Vendor grants Customer, its Affiliates, and contractors acting on their behalf a worldwide, non-exclusive right during the subscription term to access and use the hosted Services and documentation for their internal business purposes and to provide services to Customer. Customer may permit Authorized Users to exercise those rights.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-13.2","number":"13.2","heading":"For software and Vendor Technology delivered to Customer on a paid-up basis or embedded in a Deliverable, Vendor grants Customer and its Affiliates a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid licence to use, execute, reproduce, display, perform, modify, create derivative works from, and permit contractors to support that material for Customer's business.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-13.3","number":"13.3","heading":"Customer may transfer its licence rights to an Affiliate or successor in connection with an assignment permitted by Section 24. Vendor shall not revoke or suspend a licence except during a material uncured payment or use breach affecting the licensed item, after notice and a reasonable opportunity to cure.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-13.4","number":"13.4","heading":"Customer shall not knowingly reverse engineer hosted source code except to the extent a restriction is prohibited by Applicable Law, interfere with the Services, bypass documented security controls, or use the Services to violate Applicable Law. These restrictions do not limit testing authorized by the security exhibit or use of Customer Data and output.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-14","number":"14","heading":"INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY AND DELIVERABLES","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-14.1","number":"14.1","heading":"As between the Parties, Customer owns all Customer Data, Customer Confidential Information, Customer-provided material, and intellectual property Customer owned or developed independently of the Services. No right transfers to Vendor except the limited right to process that material solely to provide, secure, support, and improve the Services for Customer.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-14.2","number":"14.2","heading":"Vendor exclusively owns every Deliverable created for Customer. Customer receives a revocable, non-transferable licence to use a Deliverable only during the applicable Order Form term.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-14.3","number":"14.3","heading":"Vendor retains Vendor Technology. To the extent Vendor Technology is incorporated in or required to use a Deliverable, the perpetual licence in Section 13.2 applies. Vendor shall identify material Vendor Technology in a Deliverable before delivery and may not incorporate third-party material that materially restricts Customer's intended use without written approval.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-14.4","number":"14.4","heading":"No jointly owned intellectual property is created unless the Parties sign a separate instrument identifying it and their exploitation rights. Feedback is voluntary; Vendor may use generalized suggestions without identifying Customer or disclosing Customer Confidential Information, and Customer retains the unrestricted right to use its own feedback.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-15","number":"15","heading":"CUSTOMER DATA AND PRIVACY","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-15.1","number":"15.1","heading":"Vendor shall process Customer Data only on Customer's documented instructions, to provide the Services, and as permitted by this Agreement. Vendor shall not sell Customer Data, use it for advertising, combine it with another customer's identifiable data, or train a generally available model on it without Customer's express written consent.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-15.2","number":"15.2","heading":"Each Party shall comply with Applicable Law concerning personal information. If Vendor processes personal information for Customer, the Parties' data-processing addendum is incorporated. Vendor is a processor or service provider and shall assist Customer with data-subject requests, impact assessments, consultations, and regulatory inquiries.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-16","number":"16","heading":"CONFIDENTIALITY","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-16.1","number":"16.1","heading":"“Confidential Information” means non-public information disclosed by or for a Party that is marked confidential or that a reasonable recipient would understand to be confidential given its nature and the circumstances. Customer Data, security information, product plans, pricing, personnel data, and the terms of this Agreement are Confidential Information whether or not marked.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-16.2","number":"16.2","heading":"The recipient shall use Confidential Information only to perform or exercise rights under this Agreement, protect it with at least reasonable care, and disclose it only to personnel, Affiliates, advisers, and subcontractors who need to know and are bound by confidentiality obligations. The recipient is responsible for their unauthorized use or disclosure.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-16.5","number":"16.5","heading":"On request or termination, the recipient shall return or destroy Confidential Information, subject to routine backups and legal retention. Duties for trade secrets continue while protected as trade secrets; duties for other Confidential Information continue for five years after disclosure. Customer Data remains governed by Sections 11 and 15.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-17","number":"17","heading":"INFORMATION SECURITY","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-17.1","number":"17.1","heading":"Vendor shall maintain a written information-security program using administrative, technical, organizational, and physical safeguards appropriate to the sensitivity of Customer Data and risk. At minimum, Vendor shall implement least-privilege access, multifactor authentication, encryption in transit and at rest, secure development, vulnerability management, logging, backup, business continuity, and annual workforce training.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-17.2","number":"17.2","heading":"Vendor shall notify Customer without undue delay and no later than twenty-four hours after confirming unauthorized access to, acquisition, disclosure, alteration, loss, or destruction of Customer Data or a material compromise of systems used to provide the Services (a “Security Incident”). Notice will include known facts, affected data and systems, containment, and a contact.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-18","number":"18","heading":"INSURANCE","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-18.1","number":"18.1","heading":"Vendor shall maintain, at its own expense throughout the term and for one year afterward, commercial general liability insurance of at least USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 aggregate, workers' compensation as required by law, employer's liability of USD 1,000,000, professional errors and omissions insurance of USD 2,000,000, and cyber and privacy liability insurance of USD 5,000,000.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-18.2","number":"18.2","heading":"Policies will be issued by reputable insurers and be primary to Customer's insurance where commercially customary. On request, Vendor shall provide certificates of insurance and evidence of relevant coverage. Vendor shall give advance notice of cancellation or material reduction to the extent available from its insurer. Insurance does not limit Vendor's liabilities.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-19","number":"19","heading":"WARRANTIES","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-19.1","number":"19.1","heading":"Vendor warrants that Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner by qualified personnel, in accordance with industry standards, this Agreement, and each Order Form. Vendor further warrants that Services and Deliverables will materially conform to their documentation and agreed specifications.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-19.2","number":"19.2","heading":"For ninety days after delivery or acceptance, whichever is later, each Deliverable will materially conform to its documentation and acceptance criteria. Hosted Services will conform throughout the subscription term. Vendor warrants it has authority to enter the Agreement and grant the rights stated here.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-19.3","number":"19.3","heading":"Vendor warrants the Services and Deliverables will not contain malicious code intentionally introduced by Vendor, and that Vendor will comply with Applicable Law. Vendor will not materially diminish functionality during a term or use open-source software in a way that requires disclosure or licensing of Customer source code.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-19.4","number":"19.4","heading":"For breach of Section 19.1 or 19.2, Vendor shall promptly re-perform, repair, or replace the nonconforming item at no charge. If Vendor cannot do so within a reasonable period, Customer may terminate the affected item and receive a refund of Fees paid for it. This remedy is not exclusive for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security, or indemnified claims.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-19.5","number":"19.5","heading":"Except for the express warranties in this Agreement, neither Party makes an implied warranty to the maximum extent lawful. No disclaimer limits an express warranty, service level, indemnity, confidentiality duty, data-protection duty, or remedy expressly provided here.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-21","number":"21","heading":"LIMITATION OF LIABILITY","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-21.1","number":"21.1","heading":"Except for Excluded Claims, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of the Fees paid or payable by Customer during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim and USD 1,000,000. The cap is mutual and applies regardless of the form of action or number of claims.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-21.2","number":"21.2","heading":"Except for Excluded Claims, neither Party is liable for indirect, incidental, special, exemplary, punitive, or consequential damages, or for lost profits, revenues, or goodwill, to the extent those damages are legally excludable. Costs of restoring Customer Data, obtaining replacement services, required notices, and reasonable incident response are direct damages.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-21.3","number":"21.3","heading":"“Excluded Claims” means a Party's breach of confidentiality, data-protection, or security obligations; its indemnification obligations; gross negligence, wilful misconduct, or fraud; or infringement or misappropriation of the other Party's intellectual property. Customer's obligation to pay undisputed Fees for conforming Services is not damages and is not limited by this Section.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-21.4","number":"21.4","heading":"The limitations allocate risk between sophisticated Parties and apply only to the maximum extent permitted by Applicable Law. Nothing limits liability that cannot lawfully be limited. Each cap and exclusion is independent and survives failure of an exclusive remedy.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-22","number":"22","heading":"AUDIT RIGHTS","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-22.1","number":"22.1","heading":"Vendor may audit Customer's compliance with licence quantities no more than once in any twelve-month period, on at least thirty days' prior written notice, during normal business hours, and in a manner that does not unreasonably disrupt Customer. An audit will be conducted off-site where practicable by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-22.2","number":"22.2","heading":"Vendor bears audit costs unless the audit establishes an underpayment exceeding five percent for the audited period, in which case Customer will pay reasonable audit costs and the undisputed shortfall. Vendor and its auditor may not access Customer systems directly, Customer Data unrelated to usage, privileged material, or another supplier's confidential information.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-22.3","number":"22.3","heading":"Audit findings are Customer Confidential Information and may be used only to enforce this Agreement. Vendor shall provide a copy of the final report. Payment of a shortfall resolves the audited quantity issue absent fraud or demonstrable error.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-23","number":"23","heading":"RECORDS AND CUSTOMER ASSURANCE","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-24","number":"24","heading":"ASSIGNMENT AND CHANGE OF CONTROL","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-24.1","number":"24.1","heading":"Customer may assign this Agreement or an Order Form without Vendor's consent to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all assets or business to which the Agreement relates. Customer shall give prompt written notice, and the assignee shall assume the applicable obligations.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-24.2","number":"24.2","heading":"Vendor may not assign this Agreement, delegate material performance, or transfer it by change of control without Customer's prior written consent, not to be unreasonably withheld for an assignee with adequate capability and financial standing. Vendor may never assign to a direct Customer competitor without Customer's consent.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-24.3","number":"24.3","heading":"For other assignments, neither Party may assign without the other's prior written consent, not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed. A permitted assignment does not relieve accrued obligations. An attempted assignment contrary to this Section is void to the extent permitted by law.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-24.4","number":"24.4","heading":"Customer's change of control does not give Vendor a right to terminate, suspend, reprice, accelerate Fees, or reduce service. Vendor shall cooperate with reasonable administrative changes needed to reflect a permitted successor.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-25","number":"25","heading":"PUBLICITY AND MARKS","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-25.1","number":"25.1","heading":"Neither Party may issue a press release naming the other or use the other's names, trademarks, logos, or service marks in publicity, customer lists, case studies, or marketing without prior written consent in each instance. Customer may withdraw consent prospectively.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-26","number":"26","heading":"COMPLIANCE WITH LAW AND ETHICS","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-26.1","number":"26.1","heading":"Each Party shall comply with Applicable Law in performing this Agreement. Vendor shall maintain policies reasonably designed to prevent bribery, corruption, forced labour, discrimination, retaliation, and conflicts of interest and shall provide annual compliance training to assigned personnel.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-26.2","number":"26.2","heading":"Vendor represents it has not offered and will not offer anything of value to improperly influence an official or private person in connection with this Agreement. Vendor shall maintain accurate books and promptly report a credible suspected violation materially related to the Services.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-26.3","number":"26.3","heading":"Each Party shall comply with applicable export-control and sanctions laws. Vendor is responsible for classifying Vendor Technology and identifying restrictions before delivery. Customer will not knowingly permit access from a comprehensively sanctioned jurisdiction contrary to written notice and Applicable Law.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-26.4","number":"26.4","heading":"Vendor shall comply with reasonable Customer workplace, safety, security, and acceptable-use policies supplied in advance while accessing Customer facilities or systems. A policy does not amend commercial terms or impose obligations unrelated to that access.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-27","number":"27","heading":"FORCE MAJEURE AND BUSINESS CONTINUITY","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-27.1","number":"27.1","heading":"Neither Party is liable for delay caused by an event beyond its reasonable control that could not have been prevented through reasonable care, excluding inability to pay, staffing shortages, subcontractor failure that could reasonably be avoided, or a cyberattack preventable by required safeguards. The affected Party shall promptly notify the other and mitigate.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-27.2","number":"27.2","heading":"Vendor shall maintain and test at least annually business-continuity and disaster-recovery plans appropriate to the Services. Plans will address redundant systems, backups, recovery objectives, communications, and alternate personnel. Vendor shall provide a current executive summary on request.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-27.3","number":"27.3","heading":"If a force-majeure event materially prevents an affected Service for more than fifteen consecutive days, Customer may procure substitute services and suspend affected Fees. This process does not delay urgent relief or a filing needed to preserve a limitations period. Operational notices may be delivered through agreed service channels.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-29.2","number":"29.2","heading":"Notice is effective on documented delivery, except a refusal is deemed delivery. A Party may change its notice address by notice under this Section. Email alone is insufficient for breach, termination, indemnity, assignment, or litigation notices unless receipt is affirmatively acknowledged.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-29.3","number":"29.3","heading":"Notices to Customer must copy legal@northwind.example, and notices to Vendor must copy legal@brightline.example. content.text:
**Finding: missing (medium) — no post-termination transition assistance or data return.**

- **What the document says:** Section 10 covers only access cut-off (10.1), Deliverable delivery and refunds (10.2). Section 10.1 references "any agreed transition period" but no clause creates one.
- **Gap confirmed:** No hits for "transition" assistance obligations, "machine-readable", or any deletion language. Section 16.5 returns/destroys *Confidential Information* but expressly carves out Customer Data to "Sections 11 and 15" — Section 11 does not exist in this Agreement, and Section 15 (Customer Data and Privacy) imposes no return, export or deletion duty. So on termination we would have no contractual route to recover our data.
- **Remedy (validated, ok:true):** New Section 10.3 inserted after 10.2 with the preferred position — up to six months' transition assistance at Vendor's then-current rates, return/export of Customer Data in a commonly used machine-readable format within 30 days, and certified deletion thereafter (subject to routine backups and legal retention). Fallback of 90 days' assistance with the same 30-day export offered in the comment.

[{"id":"f-indemn-8c10665a","ruleId":"INDEMN","ruleTitle":"Indemnification by Vendor","severity":"critical","status":"missing","sectionRef":"§ 19.5 Except for the express warranties in this Agreement, neither Party makes an implied warranty to the maximum extent lawful. The cap is mutual and applies regardless of the form of action or number of claims.","rationale":"Section 21 meets our preferred position in full. 21.1 sets a single mutual cap at the greater of (a) Fees paid or payable by Customer in the 12 months preceding the claim event and (b) USD 1,000,000, expressly stated to be mutual — neither party is uncapped and the basis is \"paid or payable\" rather than the narrower \"paid\". The \"Fees\" definition (§1.5) covers recurring subscription, professional services and usage fees (not an illusory set-up fee), and §2.1 commits USD 2,000,000 of annual spend, so the fee-based limb is meaningful. 21.2 excludes indirect/consequential damages mutually and helpfully confirms data restoration, replacement services, breach notification and incident response costs are direct damages. 21.3 places confidentiality, data-protection and security breaches, indemnification obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and infringement of the other party's IP outside the cap, and confirms Customer's obligation to pay undisputed Fees is not \"damages\". No competing cap or one-sided liability language appears elsewhere (§18.2 confirms insurance does not limit Vendor's liabilities). Separate note for the indemnity rule: Section 20 (indemnification, cross-referenced in §9.3 and §21.3) is absent from the document, so the indemnity carve-out currently has nothing to attach to; that gap is outside the scope of this cap rule and no redline to Section 21 is warranted.","verification":"skipped"},{"id":"f-assign-d71c2dc8","ruleId":"ASSIGN","ruleTitle":"Assignment and change of control","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 24.1 Customer may assign this Agreement or an Order Form without Vendor's consent to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all assets or business to which the Agreement relates. {"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement

**To:** Deal team  
**From:** Legal (in-house counsel, Customer)  
**Re:** Playbook review of Vendor's Master Services Agreement — verified findings

---

## Executive summary

We reviewed the Agreement against the playbook and identified **19 findings: 13 issues (3 critical, 5 high, 5 medium) and 6 compliant provisions**. The commercial architecture is materially off-market against us in four respects.

First, **there is no indemnification section at all** — the outline jumps from Section 19 (Warranties) to Section 21 (Limitation of Liability), and no defend/indemnify/hold-harmless obligation appears anywhere, leaving dangling cross-references in §§ 9.3, 19.4, 19.5, 21.3 and 30.5. Vendor therefore owes us no IP infringement or misconduct indemnity, which is a playbook walk-away scenario. We have inserted a new Section 20.

Second, **§ 14.2 vests exclusive ownership of Deliverables we commission and pay for in Vendor** and gives us only a revocable, non-transferable licence for the Order Form term — failing both the preferred position and the fallback, and inconsistent with §§ 13.2, 13.3 and 14.3.

Third, **§ 2.1 imposes a three-year, USD 2,000,000-per-year take-or-pay commitment "without reduction or termination rights"** (USD 6,000,000 aggregate), functioning as a disguised liquidated amount equal to remaining contract value and conflicting with §§ 7.1, 12.3 and 27.3. Compounding this, **Section 9 contains no termination for convenience** despite the three-year term in § 8.1.

Fourth, the Agreement contains **a cluster of one-sided restraints on us that contradict Vendor's own acknowledgement in § 12.3**: the disclose-and-match gate in § 7.2 (de facto exclusivity and reverse MFN), the worldwide 24-month non-compete in § 12.4, and the 24-month no-hire in § 12.4.

Separately, **§ 28.1 selects Singapore law and exclusive Singapore jurisdiction** and directly conflicts with the New York County jurisdiction clause in § 28.2, and there is **no transition assistance or Customer Data return/deletion obligation** anywhere (§ 16.5 carves Customer Data out to "Sections 11 and 15", but Section 11 does not exist and Section 15 contains no return or deletion duty).

On the positive side, the limitation of liability (§ 21), assignment and change of control (§ 24), audit rights (§ 22), auto-renewal (§ 8.2–8.3), performance warranty (§ 19) and Vendor insurance (§ 18) all meet or exceed our preferred positions and require no redline.

---

## Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Issue / position taken |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Missing | Gap between §§ 19 and 21; cross-refs at §§ 9.3, 19.4, 19.5 (quoted), 21.3, 30.5 | No indemnity anywhere. Inserted new Section 20: Vendor defence/indemnity for third-party IP, breach of law, Vendor-caused Customer Data incidents, gross negligence/wilful misconduct; standard claim procedure; procure/modify/replace/refund remedies (curing the § 9.3 reference); narrow Customer indemnity. No super-cap needed — § 21.3 already treats indemnification as an Excluded Claim. |
| 2 | Critical | IP — Ownership of Deliverables and Customer Data | Deviation | § 14.2 | Vendor owns all Deliverables; we get only a revocable, term-limited licence. Reversed ownership to Customer with Vendor assignment; Vendor Technology retained under §§ 14.3 / 13.2. §§ 14.1 and 14.4 are compliant. |
| 3 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Cap, mutuality and carve-outs | Compliant | § 21.1 (with §§ 21.2, 21.3, 1.5, 2.1, 18.2) | Single mutual cap at the greater of 12 months' Fees "paid or payable" and USD 1,000,000; mutual consequential-loss exclusion with restoration/notification costs confirmed direct; confidentiality, data protection/security, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement carved out. No redline. |
| 4 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | § 24.1 (with §§ 24.2–24.4, 13.3) | Customer may assign to Affiliate or successor without consent; Vendor bound asymmetrically including change-of-control consent and competitor bar; § 24.4 removes Vendor termination/repricing on our change of control. No redline. |
| 5 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Deviation | § 7.2 | Disclose-and-match gate operates as de facto exclusivity with no category, duration or performance-based limit, and contradicts § 12.3. Deleted; narrow fallback (single category, 12 months, auto-termination on missed service levels) offered in comment. |
| 6 | High | LD — Liquidated damages / penalties payable by Customer | Deviation | § 2.1 | Take-or-pay "without reduction or termination rights" is a disguised Customer-payable liquidated amount equal to remaining contract value (USD 6,000,000), conflicting with §§ 7.1, 12.3 and 27.3. Removed; confirmed no take-or-pay, penalty, LDs or early-termination amount payable by Customer, with a three-months'-Fees fallback. |
| 7 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § 14.2 (cf. §§ 13.1–13.3) | Deliverable licence is revocable, non-transferable, term-limited and excludes Affiliates and contractors, conflicting with the bargain in §§ 13.2–13.3. Aligned 14.2 to perpetual, irrevocable, transferable terms extending to Affiliates and contractors. |
| 8 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Deviation | § 12.4 (second) | Worldwide, undefined-scope non-compete for 24 months post-term covering development, marketing, sale and acquisition — past the walk-away line and contrary to § 12.3. Deleted; no replacement needed as § 12.3 preserves freedom to operate. |
| 9 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Missing | § 9 (Termination); cf. §§ 8.1, 2.1 | Cause-based rights only, against a three-year term and a take-or-pay commitment expressly excluding termination rights. Added § 9.4: Customer convenience termination on 30 days' notice with pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees; no Vendor convenience right during a committed term; § 2.1 conformed. |
| 10 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 22.1 (with §§ 22.2, 22.3) | Once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, business hours, off-site where practicable via independent auditor; Vendor bears cost absent >5% underpayment; no direct system access; findings are our Confidential Information. No redline. |
| 11 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Deviation | § 28.1 (conflicts with § 28.2) | Singapore law and exclusive Singapore jurisdiction is outside the accepted list and conflicts with New York County jurisdiction in § 28.2. Replaced with New York law and New York County courts. No arbitration clause elsewhere. |
| 12 | Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation burdening Customer | Deviation | § 7.2 | Reverse MFN requiring us to disclose and match better third-party offers — walk-away position; contradicts § 12.3. Deleted; no Vendor-granted MFN exists elsewhere. |
| 13 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | Deviation | § 2.1 | Three-year USD 2,000,000/year take-or-pay without reduction or termination rights, contrary to § 12.3. Replaced with fees for Services ordered or used only; 12-month reducible true-up fallback offered. |
| 14 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Deviation | § 12.4 | One-sided 24-month no-hire covering all Vendor employees "regardless of how the employee applies", with no general-advertising carve-out; contradicts § 12.3. Deleted; mutual 12-month non-solicit with carve-outs offered as fallback. |
| 15 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Compliant | § 8.2 (with §§ 8.1, 8.3) | Twelve-month renewals, 30-day opt-out, 60-day Vendor reminder with deadline extension if not sent; uplifts capped at lesser of CPI and 3% on 90 days' notice. No redline. |
| 16 | Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | Missing | § 10.1; § 16.5 (carve-out to non-existent Section 11 and to Section 15) | No transition assistance and no Customer Data return, export or deletion-certification obligation. Inserted new § 10.3: up to 6 months' assistance at then-current rates, return in a commonly used machine-readable format within 30 days, certified deletion thereafter (fallback: 90 days' assistance, same 30-day export). |
| 17 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Compliant | § 19.1 (with §§ 19.2–19.5, 17) | Professional/workmanlike and conformity warranties; 90 days for Deliverables and full subscription term for hosted Services; malicious code and Applicable Law warranties; re-performance escalating to termination and refund, expressly non-exclusive. Disclaimer in § 19.5 limited to implied warranties. No redline. |
| 18 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Compliant | § 18.1 (with § 18.2) | CGL USD 1M/2M, workers' compensation, employer's liability USD 1M, E&O USD 2M, cyber/privacy USD 5M, term plus one year; certificates, primary coverage, cancellation notice; insurance does not cap liability. No redline. |

---

## Walk-away items

These are at or beyond our walk-away thresholds and should be treated as conditions of signature rather than negotiating currency:

1. **Absence of any Vendor indemnity (new Section 20).** No IP infringement or misconduct indemnity anywhere in the Agreement is the playbook walk-away scenario, and §§ 9.3 and 21.3 already assume one exists.
2. **§ 2.1 take-or-pay.** A liquidated amount equal to the remaining contract value (USD 6,000,000) payable "without reduction or termination rights", including after we terminate for Vendor breach, exceeds the walk-away threshold under both the LD and MINCOMMIT rules.
3. **§ 12.4 non-compete.** A post-term non-compete exceeding 12 months with an undefined "competes with Vendor" scope is past the walk-away line.
4. **§ 7.2 reverse MFN / disclose-and-match.** An open-ended obligation to extend better third-party terms to Vendor is the walk-away position; MFN is acceptable only in our favour.
5. **§ 12.4 no-hire.** A no-hire covering all Vendor personnel for 24 months with no unsolicited-approach or general-advertising carve-out sits at the walk-away line.
6. **§ 28.1 Singapore law and exclusive Singapore venue.** Outside the accepted list and approaching the walk-away position on exclusive foreign venue; it also conflicts irreconcilably with § 28.2.

---

## Next steps

1. **Issue the redline** as marked: new Section 20 (indemnification); reversal of Deliverable ownership and licence terms in § 14.2; deletion of § 7.2 and both limbs of § 12.4; removal of the § 2.1 take-or-pay; new § 9.4 (Customer convenience termination); new § 10.3 (transition assistance and data return/deletion); and New York law and venue in § 28.1.
2. **Flag the internal inconsistencies to Vendor** as a drafting matter to accelerate agreement: § 12.3 already disclaims the exclusivity, MFN, minimum-volume and no-hire commitments that §§ 7.2 and 12.4 purport to impose; § 27.3 promises termination "without penalty" against § 2.1; § 28.1 conflicts with § 28.2; § 16.5 cross-refers to a non-existent Section 11; and §§ 9.3, 19.4, 19.5, 21.3 and 30.5 cross-refer to indemnity obligations that do not exist. § 2.2's precedence ladder does not resolve conflicts internal to the Agreement.
3. **Confirm our fallbacks** with the business before the next exchange: 12-month reducible minimum with true-up (§ 2.1); three-months'-Fees early-termination fee if a commitment is unavoidable; 90 days' transition assistance with the same 30-day export; and, if a restraint is genuinely required, a single-named-product, term-only non-compete and a mutual 12-month non-solicit with general-advertising carve-outs.
4. **Preserve the compliant clauses.** Sections 18, 19, 21, 22, 24 and 8.2–8.3 meet or exceed our positions; we should not reopen them, and we should ensure Vendor's counter-draft does not narrow the § 21.3 carve-outs, § 24.4 or the § 19.5 anti-swallowing language when it responds on indemnity.
5. **Escalate if the walk-away items are refused.** We recommend deal-team and sponsor sign-off before proceeding on any draft that retains the § 2.1 take-or-pay or omits a Vendor indemnity.

*Note: verification of these findings was skipped in this pass; conclusions are based on the drafting as recorded above and should be re-confirmed against the executed draft before signature.*"}
